Q001.N1.body: the hall, entry: quest start He has Ciri intel and says so immediately; he wants a "small favor": find his wife and daughter, who he says were kidnapped. > "Kidnapped by whom?" [gate: none] -> BARON_LIE (he performs bafflement) > "What aren't you saying?" [gate: none] -> BARON_LIE (same node, he holds) > "Deal." [gate: none] -> INVESTIGATE unlocks NOVERB: "I'll pay you for the intel instead." Geralt cannot buy his way out of the story. The intel is not for sale, only for work. COST: nothing yet. The lie is free the first time. That's what makes it a lie.
Q001.N1.title: NODE BARON_MEET

Q001.N2.body: after the bedrooms, entry: knows:fight_signs (Witcher senses found the struggle, the hidden liquor, Tamara's letter) THE NODE THE QUEST IS BUILT ON. Same room, same man, different text because of what you LEARNED. (Q125 W7's mechanic, four years earlier.) > "There was a fight. She left. Nobody took her." [gate: knows:fight_signs] -> BARON_BREAKS > "Tell me about the drinking." [gate: knows:liquor] -> BARON_DEFLECTS (loops) > (press on Tamara's letter) [gate: has:letter] -> BARON_BREAKS TRAP: "Fine, kidnapped. Where do I start?" [gate: none] — accepting his frame. Available, functional, wrong: it costs you BARON_BREAKS this scene; the truth arrives later and flatter. WHAT BREAKS HIM: not accusation. EVIDENCE. He folds the moment the frame can't hold, and then he tells you about the pregnancy, and then the quest hands you the botchling.
Q001.N2.title: NODE BARON_CONFRONT

Q001.N3.body: the grave, entry: knows:botchling The Pellar has told you: the thing can be killed as a monster, or NAMED and buried as a child, which turns it into a lubberkin that will lead you to Anna. > "We name it." [gate: none] -> NAMING (the Baron carries it; interruptible ambushes en route; he does not put it down) > "We kill it." [gate: none] -> FIGHT (harder, faster, and the trail to Anna still resolves via other means, colder) NOVERB: "You carry it. I'll wait here." — does not exist for the BARON. He cannot delegate the carrying. The game gives HIM no options during the walk; his hands are full of his crime, and the player fights off wraiths AROUND him. The removed verb belongs to an NPC, and it is the best staging in the game.
Q001.N3.title: NODE BOTCHLING_CHOICE

Q001.N4.body: Oxenfurt, entry: found her She is safe, housed, and joining the witch hunters. > "Your father wants you home." [gate: none] -> TAMARA_NO (she itemizes the beatings, calmly) > "He's changed." [gate: none] TRAP -> TAMARA_NO (she has heard "changed" before; costs Geralt credibility in her next line) > "Your mother's still out there." [gate: none] -> TAMARA_PIVOT (this she'll act on; not for him, for Anna) LOCKS: nothing. She cannot be argued into anything. THE POINT: this node has no winning line. It exists so the player experiences a conversation where persuasion is not on the menu at all.
Q001.N4.title: NODE TAMARA_MEET

Q001.N5.body: the hall, endgame of this file (resolution completes in Q4's fork) What he asks for, at the end, is not forgiveness. It's the next task. He will go get Anna himself. > "She may not want saving by you." [gate: none] -> he knows. He goes anyway. > (say nothing) [gate: none] SILENCE -> same. The quest stops offering the player leverage over him; his arc has left the player's hands.
Q001.N5.title: NODE BARON_VERDICT

Q002.N1.body: the hinge conversation, entry: enough evidence to name him THE FAMOUS ONE. Mortimer can be confronted, joined, blackmailed, or bypassed entirely. > "I know what you're planning." [gate: knows:plot] -> M_CONFRONT (he denies, quest continues hostile) > "I want in." [gate: none] TRAP+DOOR -> M_JOIN (opens the cannibal branch; this trap is a REAL DOOR, the rarest kind) > "The Society will hear about this." [gate: knows:plot] -> M_FLIGHT (he flees; the Society investigates itself) > [Barter 45] "Heritage is expensive. Pay me." [gate: barter>=45] -> M_BRIBE NOTE FOR THE COMPILE: FNV gates on SKILLS (Barter/Speech), not karma. Bohemia's .bq bans stat gates entirely; the port converts every skill gate here into a KNOWLEDGE or DEED gate. The quest loses nothing: every skill gate in Beyond the Beef has a non-skill route around it. THAT is the FNV design lesson — the stat check is a shortcut, never the only key.
Q002.N1.title: NODE MORTIMER_HINGE

Q002.N2.body: entry: found Ted > "Your father sent me. Let's go." [gate: none] -> ESCORT (the safe route) > "Stay put. I end this first." [gate: none] -> TED_WAITS (opens the resolutions that need the kitchen) > (leave him) [gate: none] SILENCE -> TED_STAYS_MEAT (the door to B5) NOVERB: "It's going to be okay." Ted is not offered comfort by the game. He is offered EXITS. FNV's tone in one removed verb.
Q002.N2.title: NODE FREEZER_TED

Q002.N3.body: the kitchen, entry: Ted out + a body needed The quest will let you replace Ted's corpse with another corpse, and the other corpse can be CARLYLE ST. CLAIR, an innocent man, lured and murdered by you for the purpose. > (lure St. Clair) [gate: none] TRAP-THAT-IS-A-PLAN -> B5 opens THE CRAFT FINDING: the game's most evil branch requires the most PLAYER INITIATIVE. Nobody suggests it. No NPC plants it. You have to assemble it from parts, on purpose. Evil as a crafting recipe. Cross-ref Q126 W6 (the cruelest option is unmarked); this is the elaborated version: the cruelest option is UNWRITTEN and the player authors it.
Q002.N3.title: NODE THE_SUBSTITUTION

Q002.N4.body: entry: resolution reached Same node, six different texts, depending on WHAT you tell him and WHETHER Ted is alive and WHAT Ted saw. > truth + Ted alive -> caps, gratitude, no embargo > lie + Ted alive [gate: ted_coached] -> caps, and the lie holds only if you coached Ted first (a DEPENDENT lie — the game checks the witness) > Ted dead + framed story -> grief converts to the embargo threat; the Strip's food supply enters the ending slides THE MECHANIC TO STEAL: THE LIE HAS A WITNESS REQUIREMENT. You cannot just say it; you have to have ARRANGED it. Bohemia's .bq expresses this as [gate: flag:coached_witness] on the lie option — a lie that requires prep is a lie the player COMMITS to, not one they stumble into.
Q002.N4.title: NODE HECK_PAYOUT

Q003.N3.body: the fork, entry: data in hand, gas vented or not The quest's whole weight lands on a menu with no NPC in the room. > [UPLOAD to Hildern] [gate: none] -> B1/B2 path. Caps. And the ending acknowledges what the OSI does with hungry science. > [DELETE] [gate: none] -> B3 path. Keely's way. Hildern stiffs you. > [Science 70: copy the SAFE subset] [gate: science>=70] -> B4. The "have it both ways" gate. COMPILE NOTE: again FNV's skill gate, again with a workaround (persuading Keely via her own data exists as a Speech route in the wider quest). Bohemia conversion: the "safe subset" becomes a DEED gate — you can only extract the safe subset if you BURNED THE NEST FLOOR (flag), i.e. the careful path is earned by prior thoroughness, not by a character sheet. THE STAGING FINDING: the biggest moral choice in the quest is made ALONE, at a terminal, with both advocates offstage. Cross-ref Q119 (PLAY/DELETE alone) — this is the pattern's origin point in the questbook. Bohemia uses it deliberately: the Fold's worst decisions get NO audience.
Q003.N3.studyTitle: THERE STANDS THE GRASS / VAULT 22 (Fallout: New Vegas)

Q004.N1.body: the cave under the tree, entry: sent by the Crones A voice, a heartbeat in the dark, a horse skull. It knows why you came and bids before you speak. > "The Crones sent me to kill you." [gate: none] -> S_COUNTER (it makes the orphan offer) > "What are you?" [gate: none] -> S_DRUID_STORY (the unverifiable claim) > "Prove it." [gate: none] -> S_NOPROOF — THE NODE THAT MAKES THE QUEST. It cannot prove it. It says so. The game REFUSES to sell certainty at any skill level, any sign, any dialogue depth. There is no Axii option, no Witcher-senses tell, no lore book that settles it. > (attack) [gate: none] -> FIGHT (3b) NOVERB: "Let me come back after I've checked." — SEE STAGE 5's loophole: you physically CAN leave and return (the timing exploit), but no dialogue supports it. The system permits what the conversation won't name. Bank the gap: system-honesty vs conversation-framing.
Q004.N1.title: NODE SPIRIT_OFFER

THE FUNCTION: the matrix is the WEAPONS CACHE. Every fact is a lure or a frame. The conversation phase IS the loot phase. Q014.N1.body: entry: invitation accepted, mask on A party as a dialogue system: every guest node is optional, unmarked, and cumulative toward IDENTIFYING which sister is the target. > (ask a guest about the sisters) [gate: none] -> hint (color-coded gossip: who drinks, who flirts, who funds) > (find the guest list / diary upstairs) [gate: none, trespass risk] -> hard evidence > (ask a sister directly, flattering her) [gate: knows:her_vanity] -> she may CONFIRM HERSELF to a charming stranger. The target can be talked into identifying herself at her own death-party. The best single node in the mission. THE WALK LOADS THE TALK again (Q9's law) — but here the "walk" is ITSELF conversation. The gossip matrix from Q7, dressed for a ball.
Q014.N1.title: NODE THE_FLOOR

Q014.N2.body: the cellar, entry: he recognizes the assassin's purpose > "Why should I trust you?" [gate: none] -> B_PLEADS (love, he says; the word does a lot of unexamined work) > "Deal." [gate: none] -> the non-lethal branch opens: deliver her UNCONSCIOUS to his boat. > "No." [gate: none] -> knife/exile-by-other-means remain. NOVERB: "What happens to her after?" — CANNOT BE ASKED. The game withholds the aftermath question at the exact node where a decent person would ask it, and the LOW-CHAOS meter will score the kidnapping as the CLEAN option. The system's arithmetic and the scene's ethics point in opposite directions ON PURPOSE (the designers have owned this reading): "non-lethal" is not "moral," and the score that says otherwise is the indictment. THE QUESTBOOK'S SHARPEST CASE AGAINST OUTCOME-SCORING: even a good meter (chaos, which is systemic, not moral) gets read as a conscience by players, and the game exploits the misread. Bohemia: no meter, so no misread to exploit — Bohemia's version must build the discomfort into the AFTERMATH instead (a later letter in the Fold, unsigned, in her hand

Q082.P2.body: the top port, three ports fused. (a) Our AMALGAMATION holds edited records of the dead; VS asks what happens when an institution edits a LIVING person's record and hands it back to them as their own life — his worst act, rewritten as his worst wound, producing a perfect instrument. That's a Bohemia character (a Network asset, a dynast, an Amalgamation-shaped person) waiting to be built. (b) And the craft rule that makes it land is Shadowheart's (Q76) confirmed as a LAW: what survives the edit is the truth — "the only thing that defines him is his regret... whether they died by his hand or not." The conscience is real even when the memory is fake. That IS our [READ]: evidence over testimony. (c) And STEAL the mechanical fusion: REMEMBERING IS THE PROGRESSION SYSTEM. Ashley levels up by recovering his past. Our fold + [READ] could make a dynast's capability curve literally the recovery of what was done to their family (ties our Amalgamation + Network + recorded-vs-unrecorded + [READ] + fold + standing + conscience system, Shadowheart Q76, SOMA Q34, FFXII Q80; a top-tier on-theme port).

Q087.P2.body: the top port, four ports fused. Our roguelite currently thinks about death as a RUN ENDING. Outward's answer is better and more on-theme for a dynasty: LOSING DOESN'T STOP THE STORY, IT BENDS IT. A dynast who loses a fight wakes up: stripped of goods, conscripted into a faction's labor, dumped across the valley, in medical debt, hostage, or occasionally RESCUED by someone who now wants something. The cost is TIME (our 120-BPM tick, our supply clocks, our quest deadlines) — and time is exactly what a three-generation game has to spend. Q089.P2.body: the top thematic port. Kobo Abe's metaphor is the best articulation of our stance we've found: early humans used STICKS to ward off threats and ROPES to bring things closer, and MOST GAMES ARE STICKS. Our Pacifist Law is currently a RULE ("you can finish without killing"). Death Stranding makes it a PHILOSOPHY WITH A VERB: the game's actions are ropes — carrying, connecting, building, delivering. Bank it: Bohemia's core verbs should be rope-verbs (rebuild, supply, connect, remember, carry) and the stick should be the exception that feels wrong. That also directly answers Arcanum's XP-curve flaw (Q86) — if the game's VERBS aren't violence, the progression can't reward it (ties our PACIFIST LAW + city-builder + logistics + conscience system + ART PHILOSOPHY + combat dial, Arcanum Q86, Undertale Q28).

Q089.P3.body: the standout mechanical port, and it pairs exactly with Dragon's Dogma's Pawns (Q84) and PZ's Skill Journal (Q88). Three separate teardowns now converge on the same answer for us: OUR FOLD'S INHERITANCE SHOULD BE PHYSICAL THINGS LEFT IN THE WORLD. Not a stat carryover — a LADDER. Generation one's dynast bolts a walkway across a gap, caches medicine in a wall, leaves a note, wires a generator. Generation three FINDS IT and doesn't know who left it (or does, and that's the emotion). And the Dark Souls contrast is the design rule: a MESSAGE says "try jumping"; an OBJECT lets you jump. Ours should be objects. Zero server cost, fits the single HTML file, and it's our whole theme — the dead helping the living (ties our FOLD + generational persistence + persistence-v1 + city-builder + district + prefab factory + [READ] + AMALGAMATION + single-file-carry, Dragon's Dogma Q84, Project Zomboid Q88; a top-tier port).

Q090.P5.body: the production port. In a genre that procedurally generates everything, Unknown Worlds hand-built the entire seabed because "YOU CAN'T TEACH AN ALGORITHM ART DIRECTION" — and shipped the best-looking survival game ever made, at the cost of five years, $10M, and multiple near-bankruptcies. Q091.P3.body: the antagonist port. Gwyn didn't save the world; he was TERRIFIED of what came after him, so he burned himself to delay his own successors, then had his children "shepherd the humans" — i.e. CONVINCE US TO DO IT TOO. The Way of White is a church whose one doctrine is volunteering for the furnace. And the prophecy that drives the whole game is a vague employment ad, backed by a goddess who's an illusion. For us: our founding myth (who saved Vegas, who built the Amalgamation, what the Network is FOR) should be authored by the party that benefits, and the faction that preaches sacrifice should be the recruiter. Q092.P2.body: the top port, three fused, and it's aimed straight at a currency we already have. Our three currencies are MEDICINE, electricity, resources. Bloodborne asks the question we should be asking: WHO CONTROLS THE MEDICINE, AND WHAT DOES CONTROLLING IT DO TO THEM? Yharnam's answer: an institution that discovered a miracle, monopolized the supply, KNEW it caused the plague, kept distributing it because "the common people were expendable," and then sold the ARMED RESPONSE to the consequences it created. And the definitive description of it — "'HEALTH' FOR THE CHURCH IS SIMPLY PROLONGING THE DAMAGE TO KEEP THE DESPERATE DEPENDENT ON 'TREATMENT' ANOTHER DAY" — is a faction thesis we could write tomorrow. In post-collapse Vegas, whoever holds the medicine holds everything (ties our MEDICINE currency + survival accounting + CHURCH + NETWORK + faction web (13 factions) + AMALGAMATION + death-math + logistics + district + post-economic-collapse premise; a top-tier port).

Q092.P3.body: the writing-method port. Miyazaki wrote a game whose CHARACTERS ARE INSTITUTIONS: Byrgenwerth, the Healing Church, the Choir, the School of Mensis, the Vilebloods, the Executioners. Each is a POSITION on one question (what do we do with the blood?), and their disagreements ARE the plot. We have THIRTEEN factions and a central question (what do we do with the Amalgamation / the dead / the record?). Bank the law: each faction should be a coherent ANSWER to that question, with a founding, a schism, a doctrine, and a body count — and their argument should BE our story (ties our faction web (13 factions) + AMALGAMATION + Network + Church + [READ] + GDD structure).

Q092.P4.body: the port nobody would predict. Under the gothic wallpaper, Bloodborne is about PREGNANCY AND PROGENY: gods that "all yearn for a child," women impregnated under a blood moon, umbilical cords eaten to ascend, a mother reduced to "a shell with a damaged mind," and a final ending where you become an INFANT. And the Hunter's Dream itself was "created by the Moon Presence IN ORDER TO SELECT AND NURTURE POTENTIAL CANDIDATES CAPABLE OF BECOMING ITS CHILD" — the whole game was an audition to be someone's baby. Punk: our FOLD is three generations and our AMALGAMATION is made of the dead. Bloodborne is the horror version of our premise — what if the thing that outlives you is a child you didn't choose, shaped by something that was selecting for it the whole time? (ties our FOLD + generational persistence + AMALGAMATION + Network + death-math + Liberate/Respect/Become, Dragon's Dogma Q84, Dark Souls Q91).

Q098.P3.body: the antagonist port, and it's brutal. Isidor — the town's only doctor, your teacher, the man whose letters called you home — went into the steppe with Simon Kain, DUG A HOLE, and deliberately infected himself to carry the plague back, because they'd decided "**THE PLAGUE WAS A NECESSARY STEP IN THE EVOLUTION OF THE TOWN.**" He'd already sealed a neighborhood and let it die once; the orphans you spend the whole game trying to save are the children he made. A scripted catastrophe that can't soft-lock you. (b) The haunting attacks LIGHT and NAVIGATION, and a real player's real fear was "**I am worried I will run out of blood**" — no combat, and he's terrified of his resource bar. That's our survival accounting doing horror work. (c) And the objectives are **a washing machine, a boiler room key, a generator, and an elevator.** Building maintenance inside a murder house. Q099.P7.body: bank the beat, it's the best one here. "**THIS QUEST CONTAINS THE ONLY MOMENT OF TRUE DAYLIGHT IN THE ENTIRE GAME, WHEN THE PLAYER PICKS UP THE PENDANT.**" A vampire, at the end of a haunted house, walks into a warm sunlit room. It's an illusion. It vanishes the moment you take the necklace. The final scare isn't a monster — it's **grief**: showing a creature of the dark the one thing it can never have again. Punk, our game is despair with a thread of hope. Q100.P2.body: the top port, three fused, and it's the model for at least one of our thirteen. Vault City HAS what our dynasty needs: medicine, clean water, law, an Auto-Doc, a working council. It is not a hypocrisy to be exposed — **IT ACTUALLY WORKS.** And the people who make it work live outside the wall and are called SERVANTS, and **saying the other word gets you exiled.** Not doing anything. SAYING IT. And Lynette's psychology is the whole thing: they got a **Garden of Eden Creation Kit** — a magic box — and concluded they were better people; "**IF OTHERS CANNOT ACHIEVE THE SAME AS VAULT CITY, THAT MEANS THEY ARE NOT SMART OR STRONG ENOUGH.**" In a post-ECONOMIC collapse, that's every faction that came out of it holding something. Q106.P2.body: the top port, and it's the model for our whole standing system. Godwin **has** the answer, says he has it, and **"using persuasion won't help you either."** No Speech check opens him, because the thing stopping him isn't his opinion of you — it's the **seal of confession**. And what DOES work is: "**CHOOSE THE FIRST ANSWER TO EVERY QUESTION HE ASKS YOU ABOUT YOURSELF.**" Just be honest about your life to a stranger in a bar. Punk — our standing shouldn't be a bar you fill. It should be specific people with specific obligations who need to know **who you actually are**, and a build cannot fake it. And W5 is the Pacifist Law's best joke: threaten a swordfighting priest and the intimidation "**WILL ALWAYS FAIL; WHETHER HENRY CONTINUES TO FIGHT OR BACK DOWN, GODWIN WILL INVITE HIM TO THE TAVERN**" (ties our standing + conscience system + [READ] + companions + PACIFIST LAW + faction web + district + quest factory; a top-tier port).

Q106.P3.body: STEAL both, they're the craft. (a) At the tavern, drunk, Godwin rants about "**THE IMPORTANCE OF A GOOD AND ENTERTAINING SERMON**" and tears into the church for "**GREED, HYPOCRISY AND CORRUPTION,**" and tells you to read **Jan Hus**. Nothing flags it. Two hours later you have to give that sermon, and **the rant was the answer key.** Our [READ] should teach through conversations players think are flavor. (b) And the winning sermon is: **"TO SIN IS HUMAN"** — you confess your own disgraceful night from the pulpit — then **"CRITICIZE THE PRELATES BUT STAND UP FOR GODWIN."** You attack the institution and defend the flawed man in it. It only works because it's honest. That's our ART PHILOSOPHY's target: the life lesson delivered without preaching, by making the player perform it (ties our [READ] + recorded-vs-unrecorded + conscience system + companions + ART PHILOSOPHY + despair-with-a-thread-of-hope + standing + district).

THE CITY HAS ALREADY FALLEN.**" Their evidence is a ruin that looks exactly like your city. He did arithmetic, and the humane option lost. Our survival accounting should be able to produce that: a moment where mercy has a caloric price and the player can read it. (b) **Hope is a production chain** — the House of Prayer's sermon "**COSTS 20 FOOD RATIONS**" and has a two-day cooldown. Morale as an industry with an input cost is exactly our three currencies. (c) And "**THE RISE IN DISCONTENT FROM IGNORING THE PEOPLE IS MUCH LESS THAN THE RISE IN DISCONTENT IF YOU FAIL TO FOLLOW THROUGH**" — our standing should make a broken promise cost more than never speaking (ties our survival accounting + THREE CURRENCIES + MEDICINE currency + electricity + logistics + life-support buildings + city-builder + standing + conscience system + faction web + district).

Q107.P6.body: bank the pair, they're the sharpest. (a) If you fail, your people **exile** you rather than execute you, because "**EVEN THOUGH YOU WERE INCOMPETENT, THEY STILL FELT YOU DESERVED THAT MUCH**" — into -150C, without food or coal. The mercy IS the execution, and it's the exact thing you did to the thief in act one. Our fold should end a dynast that way once. (b) And the loophole: you can earn **"THE SAVIOUR"** — no deaths from harsh laws, overwork, or exposure — while **banishing people to freeze**, because "**BANISHING PEOPLE FROM THE CITY**" does "**NOT COUNT TOWARDS OR AGAINST**" it. **It's not a death if you did it outside the walls.** That's the exact loophole real institutions use, and our conscience system should refuse it: the ledger must count what happens off-property (ties our conscience system + Megaton law + no-clean-answer + fold + generational persistence + death-math + faction web + standing + district + city-builder).

Q110.P2.body: the top port, and it's aimed straight at our roguelite spine. In Kenshi you don't get a game-over. **You get carried.** "**CANNIBALS WILL ATTACK OTHER FACTIONS AND CARRY UNCONSCIOUS ORGANIC MEMBERS OF OTHER FACTIONS TO THEIR CAMP OR VILLAGE.**" And it's the world's default: "**DEFEAT IN BATTLE? SLAVERY. COMMIT A CRIME? SLAVERY. GETTING DOWNED NEAR SLAVERS EVEN IF YOU HAVEN'T DONE ANYTHING? SLAVERY!**" Our Dead Eye Dial already has a rule — no damage before the dial — and our death-math already distinguishes down from dead. This is the next question: **when a dynast loses, where do they WAKE UP?** A faction's cage, a debt, a work crew, a hospital with a bill. Losing should relocate the story, not end it (ties our death-math + fold + generational persistence + combat dial + PACIFIST LAW + faction web (13 factions) + standing + district + city-builder + persistent consequence; a top-tier port).

(a) **The friendship system is a medical system.** "**THEY ARE LIKELY TO BLEED OUT AND DIE BEFORE REGAINING CONSCIOUSNESS UNLESS THERE IS SOMEONE TO PROVIDE FIRST AID — WHICH IS WHY IT IS WISE TO ACQUIRE A COMPANION.**" You don't recruit people for banter. Q125.P12.body: Mass Effect diagnoses the facade and then makes every reply noncommittal. In Bohemia the tribunal **is a governance event**: the verdict moves the actual faction war-posture number, permanently, in the direction of whoever's argument you fed. You don't just learn it's a proxy fight — **you get to pick who wins the proxy fight, and the settlement lives with it for a generation.** Cross-ref **Q107 (Frostpunk Londoners — people you saved organizing against you)** and **Q104 (Vault 11 — a community that gave its atrocity a procedure)**.
Q125.P12.title: FIX F9 IMMEDIATELY

Q125.P14.body: [READ] / the tribunal The cut ME2 design: each admiral's specific claim individually refutable with a specific document found in the dungeon. **That is the quest Bohemia should build**, because Bohemia already has [READ] and already has a record system. Four claims. Four documents in the ruin. You find zero, one, two, three, or four. **The verdict is a tally, not a switch.** Find two of four and you get a hung tribunal, which is its own outcome with its own consequences. This also **fixes F1**: the evidence you gather is no longer an optional MacGuffin. It is the mechanism. The dungeon run is load-bearing. And the father's file is a **fifth** document — the one that refutes *all four at once* and detonates.
Q125.P14.title: System

Q125.P17.body: This is the single best argument in 125 files for Bohemia's no-karma-bar law. The moment the scene gets a score, the score contradicts the scene, and the player optimizes toward the number instead of the person. **Q121 proved the same thing with "+30 PARAGON" on a button. This is the second conviction on the same charge.** Bohemia's version: the tribunal outcome writes to **relationships and faction posture**. Nothing writes to a morality total, because there isn't one. And **F2**: no Charm gate. Which leads directly to —

Q125.P25.body: the dungeon is his mind, every document a memory returning. **Q125 sharpens it:** *order the documents so the sympathetic explanation arrives BEFORE the damning fact.* In the Bohemia ruin the dynast finds, in this order: 1. an order that was reckless 2. the stated goal, which is noble 3. the personal reason, which is love 4. the body 5. the last recorded words, which are a chore 6. **then** the technical record, which is the crime By step 6 the player already forgave him. **That is why filing it hurts.** Cross-ref **Q122 (Sinnerman)**: the horror is the clipboard, not the cross. Same technique. The paperwork lands last and the paperwork is the wound.
Q125.P25.title: Q124 (Emil) established it

Q125.P26.title: NO LOOT IN A ROOM WITH A NAMED BODY [F6, F7]

Q125.P28.body: Bohemia has three currencies (medicine, electricity, resources) and a scavenging loop that touches every room. Therefore, explicitly: > **NAMED-BODY LAW:** any room containing the corpse of a character the player knows by name contains ZERO scavengeable currency, ZERO collectibles, ZERO containers. The scavenge verb is removed in that room, not just unrewarded. Same family as **Q118 / Q122 / Q123: the game REMOVES THE VERB.** Q125 says do it for grief, not just for violence. And **F7**: **no points for the hug.** The comfort option exists, it is written well, and it pays nothing and is logged nowhere.
Q125.P28.title: LOCK THIS AS A PRODUCTION LAW

Q125.P29.title: THE SECRET DOESN'T KEEP, AND THE MAIL SAYS SO [W10]

Q125.P3.body: The player cannot present half. Against **Q98 (Isidor's body)** and **Q113 (Isidor's list)**: Pathologic hands you a corpse and a list of names with no reason attached. Bohemia hands you a corpse with a **reason attached that makes it worse.** Against **Q120 (Deionarra)**: the dead used as a component. Rael'Zorah isn't engineered to be useful — he's *voluntarily* useful, right up to the last recorded second, and that's the horror.
Q125.P3.title: One artifact. Not splittable. Not redactable

Q125.P30.body: persistent consequence / the Amalgamation / generational persistence The dynast buries the record to protect a name. **One generation later**, a message arrives from the faction rep who wanted the research: *we went back to the site ourselves. We found it. You could have shared it and been part of what comes next. Instead you'll watch.*
Q125.P30.title: System

Q125.P31.body: Which is the Amalgamation's thesis stated from the other side — the Amalgamation exists precisely because nothing anybody uploaded was ever really deleted. Cross-ref **Q119 (Mikhaila's father)**: truth as a two-button PLAY/DELETE decision made alone. Q125 adds: **DELETE doesn't work, and you find out from someone gloating in your inbox.** Cross-ref **Q116 / Q119** and **FLAW LAW 3**: this is a persistent-consequence flag spanning a generation boundary. **It needs a regression gate in `bohemia_tests.js` on day one.** Q116 shipped a flag bugged for twenty-five years. Bohemia writes the test before the content.
Q125.P31.title: Suppression is a delay, not a deletion

Q125.P33.body: dialogue scenes / relationships After the tribunal, if the dynast protected the record, they can **tell one person, privately, off the record.** An old friend of the dead. He is shocked. He keeps it. The truth gets told exactly once, to exactly one person, and it changes nothing legally and everything between two people.
Q125.P33.title: System

Q125.P34.body: Not "confess" — **confide**. It is not a choice with a consequence tree. It is a scene where you get to stop being a politician for ninety seconds. **[PENDING, Paolo's call]** — whether confiding creates a persistent risk (he might tell someone, later, in Gen 3) or whether it's a clean, safe, human moment that the game just gives you. Both are defensible. The first is more Bohemia. The second is rarer and might be worth more.
Q125.P34.title: Bohemia needs this verb

Q125.P36.body: ME2 cut four evidence-vs-admiral rebuttals and shipped a corridor shooter with the courtroom trimmed to a switch. The consequence got scoped out and the content survived, which is exactly backward. For the Bohemia tribunal: **write the four verdict states and their generational effects FIRST.** Then write the documents. Then build the ruin. If scope cuts, cut the ruin, not the tribunal. --- --- # V2 TOP-UP — 7/16/26. #125 was built v1 hours before FORMAT LAW v2 locked; this adds the missing v2 sections. # Original file untouched above. Q125.P6.body: faction reputation / naming / the 13 factions Bohemia already has factions-as-characters. Give one of them a **naming grammar** — a title that encodes belonging. Then, at the top of a quest, have a friendly NPC greet the dynast with the wrong title, warmly, without malice, because that's what the paperwork now says. No combat. No stat. **A word changed and you're out.** And then — **W3, the better half** — if the dynast wins the trial anyway, they can **keep the wrong name.** Permanently. It shows up in every subsequent greeting, every generation, and it means *I was thrown out and I came back and I kept the receipt.* The Amalgamation, of course, files people by name. **[PENDING, Paolo's call]** — whether a dynast can choose a name the Amalgamation didn't assign, and whether that's an act of freedom or an act of deletion.

Q125.W1.body: The quest sends you to find evidence, and the evidence is not a key that opens a door — it is a loaded thing that has a target, and the target is the father of the woman standing next to you. The instant you learn what it says, the fetch quest becomes a moral object. No other quest in the trilogy turns an inventory item into a decision this cleanly. **The item does not unlock the ending. The item IS the ending, and you get to not use it.**
Q125.W1.title: THE OBJECTIVE IS THE WEAPON

Q125.W10.body: Daro'Xen digs through the Alarei herself, finds the research, and sends you a note saying you should have shared it and now you'll watch from a distance. **Your discretion protected a name, not a truth.** The most mature consequence in the mission is a piece of mail confirming that suppression is a delay, not a deletion — and it arrives after the reward screen, when you thought the quest was over. ---
Q125.W10.title: THE SECRET DOESN'T STAY SECRET AND THE GAME TELLS YOU IN AN EMAIL

Q125.W2.body: She is renamed *vas Normandy* in the first thirty seconds, in a friendly greeting, by her aunt. No combat, no roll, no fail state. A word changed and she lost her home. The board's decision is telegraphed by grammar. This is the single most economical piece of writing in the mission: **the trial's outcome is announced by how someone says hello.**
Q125.W2.title: THE PUNISHMENT ARRIVES BEFORE THE VERDICT

Q125.W3.body: She keeps *vas Normandy* forever. Through the entire third game, when every other quarian is *vas Rannoch*. The thing they did to shame her became the thing she is. **A punishment the character decides to keep is worth ten speeches about resilience.**
Q125.W3.title: THE INSULT BECOMES THE IDENTITY

Q125.W4.body: The Alarei is not a level, it is an argument delivered in sequence: reckless orders, then the stated goal (retake the homeworld), then the personal logs (he did it for her), then the body, then his last message (a task assignment), then the full technical record. By the time the game asks you the question, it has already answered *why* — and the answer makes the truth harder to tell, not easier. **Structure the discovery so the motive lands BEFORE the crime does.**
Q125.W4.title: THE DUNGEON IS A CONFESSION, ORDERED

Q125.W5.body: "Destroy the main hub, bring the data to Xen and Gerrel." No apology. No I love you that isn't wrapped in an instruction. The most devastating characterization of a father in the trilogy, delivered in one recorded log, and the game never comments on it. **Let the dead reveal themselves through what they thought was urgent.**
Q125.W5.title: HIS LAST WORDS TO HIS DAUGHTER ARE A WORK ORDER

Q125.W6.body: Four admirals, four agendas, one of them presiding without recusing, none of them primarily interested in whether she did it. War party, slaver party, peace party, family friend. The verdict is a vote about the geth war. **The trial is a proxy fight, and Tali is the object being thrown.**
Q125.W6.title: THE HEARING IS A FACADE AND YOU CAN LEARN THAT BY LISTENING

Q125.W7.body: Do the optional walk and the Paragon speech becomes a different speech: not "she's a good person," but "you are abusing this hearing for political ammunition." Same button, same points, different scene. **Optional knowledge that changes the TEXT of the climax rather than unlocking a new one is the cheapest, highest-value reactivity in the genre.**
Q125.W7.title: THE LEARNING REWRITES THE CLIMAX

Q125.W8.body: Veetor spared from Cerberus in mission two. Reegar ordered to stand down instead of dying heroically. Neither flagged. Both show up in a courtroom hours later and testify — **and they beat the stat check.** You don't need Charm if you were decent to two people who couldn't help you at the time. **The best political capital in the game is people you were kind to when it wasn't useful.**
Q125.W8.title: THE BEST OUTCOME IS PURCHASED WITH MERCY YOU DIDN'T KNOW YOU WERE BANKING

Q125.W9.body: Truth: she keeps her people, loses her father's name, loses you. Lie: she keeps her father's name, loses her people, and thanks you for it, and a species war stays on the rails. Speech: costs a stat, or costs nothing, and that's the flaw. **There is no currency that converts a name into a nation, and the game refuses to invent one.**
Q125.W9.title: EVERY ENDING COSTS SOMETHING REAL AND THE COSTS ARE INCOMPARABLE

Q125.X1.body: The sharpest critique of this quest, and it's fair: the Paragon speech is an argument Shepard could have made **before ever boarding the Alarei.** It contains no information gathered on the Alarei. You do a full combat mission for an object, and the best available outcome is reached by not using the object and giving a character-reference speech instead. A player on Steam nailed it: *smoke and mirrors distraction, that's high morality in the Mass Effect universe.* The evidence is a MacGuffin whose optimal use is to be ignored.
Q125.X1.title: THE FETCH OBJECT IS OPTIONAL TO THE BEST ENDING

Q125.X10.body: Her father's conduct got his entire crew killed. She asks you to bury that to protect his name, and the game gives Shepard no dialogue to say *your father killed those people, and their families are in this room.* Players noticed. The quest wants her request to be sympathetic and so it removes the strongest argument against it. **The game should let the player make the hard argument and still lose the fight.**
Q125.X10.title: TALI'S REQUEST IS NEVER SERIOUSLY INTERROGATED

Q125.X11.body: If you asked the admirals to move toward war or toward peace, their replies are **noncommittal, regardless.** The one place the quest could have let you touch the actual political machine, it doesn't. The facade is diagnosed and never operated on.
Q125.X11.title: THE PROXY WAR RESOLVES INTO NOTHING

Q125.X12.body: Development data shows a version where **each admiral's argument was individually refutable with evidence found on the Alarei**: Raan's security claim, Koris's torture claim, Gerrel's geth-are-weakened theory, Xen's hacking premise. Four rebuttals, four discoveries, a real trial. Legion could reportedly testify **for Rael'Zorah**. That version is a courtroom. What shipped is a shooter with a cutscene at each end. **Bank the cut version; it's the design Bohemia should actually build.** ---
Q125.X12.title: CUT CONTENT WAS THE BETTER QUEST

Q125.X2.title: LAW: if the best ending doesn't use the thing the quest sent you to get, the quest is two quests taped together

Q125.X3.body: Same flaw as **Q121 (Legion: A House Divided)**, same game, same year. The dilemma is only a dilemma if you failed to invest in Charm or Intimidate. A maxed Paragon player has no choice to make; they have a button. Flaw Law 4, now with another confirmation: **a moral enforced by a stat is a puzzle, not a dilemma.**
Q125.X3.title: THE MORALITY BAR TURNS THE DILEMMA INTO A BUILD CHECK

Q125.X4.body: +30 **Paragon** for perjury. +30 **Renegade** for submitting authentic exculpatory evidence in a court proceeding. The scoring system says: lying to protect a dead war criminal's reputation is good; telling the truth to free an innocent woman is bad. That's not a nuanced position the game is arguing. It's the karma system failing to have a vocabulary for the scene it's attached to. **This is the strongest argument in the entire questbook for NO KARMA BAR in Bohemia.** Score the scene and the scene becomes a lie about itself.
Q125.X4.title: THE POINT VALUES ARE OBSCENE AND THE GAME DOESN'T KNOW IT

Q125.X5.body: The revelation that the trial is a political facade lives in **unmarked optional conversations in a plaza you can sprint through.** The entire meaning of the quest is behind a talk you're not told to have. Worse: it's a *precondition* for both good endings (it changes the speech, and it's required for the crowd rally). **Q114 is the fix: content found by WALKING, cannot be missed.**
Q125.X5.title: THEME-IN-OPTIONAL, THE ~18TH CONFIRMATION

Q125.X6.body: Veetor's fate is decided in **mission two of the game.** Reegar's survival depends on a stand-down order during a firefight where the "heroic" read is to let him fight. Neither moment signals that it will matter. This is glorious *in retrospect* and unfair *in play* — a first-time player has no mechanism for knowing that two acts of mercy are also political capital. Bank it as a virtue with a caveat: **the payoff is one of the best in the trilogy and almost nobody sees it on a blind run.**
Q125.X6.title: OPTION D IS BUILT ON TWO INVISIBLE FLAGS SET HOURS EARLIER

Q125.X7.body: A model ship collectible and 3,000 credits, harvested from the site of your friend's father's death, thirty seconds before you play his final message. The systems layer and the drama layer are not speaking. This is not fixable by writing better; it's fixable by **not putting a collectible in the room.**
Q125.X7.title: THE LOOT DESTROYS THE ROOM

Q125.X8.title: LAW FOR BOHEMIA: no loot in a scene that ends in a body the player knows by name

Q125.X9.body: The Paragon interrupt over Rael'Zorah's corpse pays five morality points for comforting a grieving friend. The game turned compassion into a pickup. It's a small thing and it's a real one: **the moment you score kindness, the player stops feeling it and starts collecting it.**
Q125.X9.title: THE +5 HUG

Q126.N1.body: What each option WRITES is what matters for the port.*

THE REGISTER: he never menaces, because the paperwork already did. > (study the brand) [gate: none] SILENCE -> he waits. He always waits. NOVERB: "I'll pay you off." — THE DEBT HAS NO CASH EQUIVALENT. Cross-ref Q108 (the favor with no market): 2nd confirmation — the corpus's strongest debts are the ones money cannot touch.
Q127.N1.title: NODE ODIMM_TERMS

Q127.N2.body: the painted world's end, entry: rose found She holds the rose. Taking it unmakes her tableau. > "Come with me. Leave this place." [gate: none] -> I_CANNOT — the rescue verb offered and DECLINED BY THE WORLD (cf. rescue-denial register): she is made of this place now > "Give me the rose. It's time." [gate: knows:her_story (the dioramas walked)] -> she yields it AWAKE — release as informed consent > (take it from her hand) [gate: none] TRAP -> it works; she fades confused; the quest completes and something in it is broken forever, unscored NOVERB: "He still loves you." — THE COMFORTING LIE ABOUT OLGIERD IS NOT AVAILABLE. The stone heart cannot be spoken around. NO COMFORT VERBS (Q126 PORT 7), 4th confirmation.
Q127.N2.title: NODE IRIS_ASK

Q127.N3.body: the mosaic, entry: tasks done > "Take him. A deal's a deal." [gate: none] -> B1. O'Dimm collects; then offers YOUR wish. The sub-node is a WORDING MINEFIELD: ask big and the grammar will eat you; the safe answers are modest and exact. THE DEVIL'S REWARD IS A LITERACY TEST. > "I challenge you for his soul." [gate: none] -> THE RIDDLE. Failure = forfeit everything. Victory condition is COMPREHENSION (the mirror, the name, the world's hints) — not stats, not swordplay. COMPREHENSION IS A BRANCH, 9th confirmation, adversarial form: the final boss is a reading test. NOVERB: "Let's renegotiate the contract." — THE TERMS DO NOT MOVE. Cross-ref Q126 OFFER_NEED (haggling as trap): with O'Dimm the haggle option doesn't even exist. The two devils bracket the design space: Raphael amused by haggling, O'Dimm beyond its reach.
Q127.N3.title: NODE THE_COLLECTION

Q127.P2.body: the Amalgamation / NETWORK contracts / .bq The Amalgamation already IS O'Dimm's filing cabinet: uploads are contracts whose grammar outlives their signers. Bohemia's version: one NETWORK contract per act whose harm is entirely in its wording, honored perfectly. The .bq gains a @CLAUSE line for contract quests — the text of the deal is content, displayed verbatim, and the quest's solution is IN the wording. [PENDING, Paolo's call.]
Q127.P2.title: System

Q127.P3.body: A dynast-adjacent figure who got EXACTLY what they asked the NETWORK for, and the getting is the ruin. No twist, no glitch: the request, honored. The Amalgamation's best horror is customer satisfaction. Cross-ref Q115 (the comforting lie): the pair covers both failure modes — the lie that recruits, and the truth that delivers.
Q127.P3.title: THE WISH THAT WORKED [W2]

Q127.P4.body: An Amalgamation memory-space (a dead person's rendered world) that the dynast must enter, walk, and then ask its inhabitant to let go of. Release requires the ghost's informed yes; taking the objective by force works and breaks something unscored. The Fold records WHICH way it went (cf. Q126 PORT 10's freely-given crown).
Q127.P4.title: THE ARCHIVE THAT MUST CONSENT TO CLOSE [W5, W6]

Q127.P5.body: If the dynast runs errands for a power, the dynast's own debt gets a ledger line and a due date. Bohemia prices the messenger.
Q127.P5.title: THE PROXY'S BRAND [F2 fixed]

Q127.P6.body: One Act-3 confrontation with no combat resolution: the win condition is comprehension banked across the whole act, and the gate is EXPENSIVE (F1's fix: the answer requires the act's full attention, validator-checked against its knows: chain). Cross-ref Q111 (ungateable-by-format): this one IS gateable — a chain of knows: flags the player assembled by playing.
Q127.P6.title: THE READING-TEST BOSS [W7, F1 fixed]

Q127.W1.body: Every catastrophe in the expansion is a wish working exactly as worded. O'Dimm's terror is grammatical — he is what happens when the universe has a legal department. Paired with #126's honest buyer: the corpus now holds both honest devils, and neither ever needs to lie.
Q127.W1.title: THE DEVIL IS A LITERALIST, NOT A LIAR

Q127.W10.body: Collected, Olgierd pays with his soul; saved, he pays by having to live as someone who did all of it and now feels again. The rescue is not a refund. The corpus's cleanest NO-CLEAN-SURFACE finale this side of Q124.
Q127.W10.title: BOTH ENDINGS COST THE SAME MAN DIFFERENTLY

Q127.W2.body: Olgierd got everything back and the caring removed — the contract's cost was delivered INSIDE its benefit. The monkey's paw with no visible twist: the wish was the curse, whole and entire.
Q127.W2.title: THE IMMORTALITY IS THE PUNISHMENT

Q127.W3.body: Fun (the brother), fortune (the feud), love (the wife): each task tours a thing Olgierd already destroyed by wishing. The fetch list is a guided walk through the debtor's wreckage.
Q127.W3.title: THE THREE WISHES ARE THREE AUTOPSIES

Q127.W4.body: Vlodimir's one night curdles in real time — appetite outliving its allotment is the whole Everec family in one beat, and O'Dimm's one-word eviction shows the leash without raising the voice.
Q127.W4.title: THE GHOST WON'T LEAVE WHEN THE PARTY ENDS

Q127.W5.body: Iris's memories as walkable dioramas: the quest stores a relationship as LEVELS. The corpus's best staging of [READ]-as-space since Q124's descent — and here the archive is a person who must consent to being closed.
Q127.W5.title: THE PAINTED WORLD IS A MARRIAGE'S FILE FORMAT

Q127.W6.body: The rose can be taken, but the quest's true version asks Iris to let go — informed, awake, on her own terms. Pre-consented truth (Q119) inverted into pre-consented ENDING.
Q127.W6.title: THE RELEASE REQUIRES HER YES

Q127.W7.body: No sword touches O'Dimm. The challenge is riddle and recognition — the player wins by having paid attention to the world's whispers. Comprehension as combat, the questbook's thesis given a boss slot.
Q127.W7.title: THE FINAL BOSS IS A READING TEST

Q127.W8.body: Win the safe branch and O'Dimm grants YOUR wish — and the scene is a literacy exam where ambition is the trap. The quest ends by making the player draft a contract opposite a literalist. Nothing in the corpus prices language higher.
Q127.W8.title: THE REWARD IS A WORDING PROBLEM

Q127.W9.body: O'Dimm never chases, never presses, never arrives early. Patience as omnipotence: the scariest thing a power can do is be comfortable with your schedule (cf. Q126 W3's unexpiring offer — the two patience designs bracket temptation and enforcement).
Q127.W9.title: THE COLLECTOR ALWAYS WAITED

Q127.X1.body: The finale's puzzle is solvable in seconds by most players (community consensus since release); the devil's checkmate resolves as a light stroll. LAW: if the final gate is comprehension, the comprehension must have been PAID FOR — the answer should require the expansion's full attention, not the room's.
Q127.X1.title: THE RIDDLE IS FAMOUSLY EASY

Q127.X10.body: The unbreakable contract's escape hinge is a floor mosaic; some players read genius, some read groan. Bank both: THE PUN CLAUSE divides rooms and that division is a tone choice, not an error.
Q127.X10.title: THE MOON CLAUSE RESOLVES AS A PUN

Q127.X2.body: The brand that starts everything costs Geralt nothing on either branch; the proxy's debt evaporates unexamined. LAW: the messenger's contract needs its own line-item.
Q127.X2.title: GERALT'S OWN PACT IS UNDER-PRICED

Q127.X3.body: The heist is excellent AND tonally adrift from wishes one and three; the middle act is a caper wedged between a ghost story and a tragedy. Bank as a scoping note, not a sin: anthology quests must decide if variety is the point.
Q127.X3.title: WISH TWO IS A DIFFERENT GENRE

Q127.X4.body: Vlodimir pilots Geralt's body around Shani all night; the quest winks. Players noticed. LAW: possession-as-comedy needs the possessed's ledger acknowledged at least once.
Q127.X4.title: THE WEDDING'S CONSENT PROBLEM IS PLAYED FOR LAUGHS

Q127.X5.body: The dioramas (the expansion's heart) can be sprinted; the finale then asks about a marriage the player didn't watch. Theme-in-optional's cousin: THEME-IN-PACING.
Q127.X5.title: IRIS'S WORLD IS SKIPPABLE AT SPEED

Q127.X6.body: Banishing him changes nothing visible in the world after; the strongest antagonist in the franchise exits without residue on either branch. LAW: even a banished devil should leave a paperwork trail.
Q127.X6.title: O'DIMM'S DEFEAT IS OPTIONAL CANON

Q127.X7.body: Olgierd's parting gift converts the tragedy's final beat into an inventory event (cf. Q125 F6's model-ship problem, softer).
Q127.X7.title: THE SABER IS A LOOT-SHAPED GOODBYE

Q127.X8.body: Some "safe" wishes are only safe per wiki; blind players get grammar-punished for generosity. LAW: literalism traps must teach their grammar in-world first (O'Dimm does — but only if you listened; borderline, banked).
Q127.X8.title: THE WISH MINEFIELD IS UNTELEGRAPHED ASYMMETRICALLY

Q127.X9.body: Warm, well-written, and structurally a cul-de-sac the finale ignores.
Q127.X9.title: SHANI'S ARC IS A ROMANCE SIDECAR ON A DAMNATION STORY

Q128.N1.body: day one, 11:30 PM, entry: the right mask at the right hour She asks a stranger to carry her heart to a mailbox. > "Why trust me?" [gate: none] -> A_BECAUSE — the mask you wear is her fiancé's face; she is trusting the SHAPE of him. The saddest gate in the corpus: access via resemblance. > "He may not answer." [gate: none] -> A_KNOWS — she has done that math nightly > (take the letter) [gate: none] DEED -> the clock owns you now: mailbox before collection time or the chain dies silently NOVERB: "Evacuate. He'd want you safe." — THE SENSIBLE ADVICE IS NOT YOURS TO GIVE. Her mother owns that line; the player is the courier of hope, not its auditor. VERB OWNERSHIP: some sentences belong to specific NPCs, and the player's absence from them is characterization.
Q128.N1.title: NODE ANJU_KITCHEN

Q128.N2.body: day two, entry: followed the Keaton mask A man's voice in a child's body, facing away. > "Anju sent this." (the letter) [gate: has:delivered] -> K_BREAKS — the pendant handed over: "give her this; tell her I will come." > "Why hide from HER?" [gate: none] -> K_SHAME — the curse he could survive; being SEEN like this he thinks he can't > (say nothing; wait) [gate: none] SILENCE -> he speaks anyway; the back of his head does the scene NOVERB: "She won't care what you look like." — THE REASSURANCE IS REMOVED. The player cannot argue him out of shame; only the SCHEDULE can — he must arrive on time as he is. Shame is not defeated by dialogue in this quest; it is defeated by APPOINTMENT-KEEPING. Bank hard: the questbook's only quest where punctuality IS the character arc.
Q128.N2.title: NODE KAFEI_BACKROOM

Q128.N3.body: day two evening, pendant delivered Her mother says leave; the pendant says stay. > (deliver the pendant) [gate: has:pendant] -> she stays. THE MIDPOINT IS HER CHOICE, NOT YOURS — the player enables a decision and does not make it (cf. Q16's spear: leverage, not control; 2nd confirmation of THE CHOICE BELONGS TO ITS OWNER).
Q128.N3.title: NODE ANJU_DECISION

Q128.P2.body: 120 BPM LAW / scheduler / bohemia_scheduler.js Bohemia's beat-quantized world is BUILT for this: one quest per act whose keys are all APPOINTMENTS on the settlement's real clock — NPC schedules the player must intersect, letters with collection beats, a door that opens once. The .bq gains time gates: [gate: clock:day2_2200]. The scheduler already ticks; this quest class makes it VISIBLE. [PENDING, Paolo's call.]
Q128.P2.title: System

Q128.P3.body: Missed links never announce; the world just reconfigures sadder. F2's fix: each broken link leaves ONE diegetic tell (an uncollected letter in the box, a light left on). The Fold logs the miss; the town doesn't.
Q128.P3.title: FAILURE AS AMBIENCE, WITH ONE TELL [W6, F2 fixed]

Q128.P4.body: The Amalgamation is resemblance at scale: portraits trusted because they wear the right face. One Bohemia quest where an NPC trusts the dynast BECAUSE of a resemblance (a mask, a coat, a dead relative's face), and the quest prices what that trust costs both parties when the resemblance is all it was. This is the file's sharpest gift to the lore.
Q128.P4.title: RESEMBLANCE-TRUST, PRICED [F8]

Q128.P5.body: Roguelite law: one artifact class per generation survives the run-reset the way the Couple's Mask survives the rewind — and (F9's fix) it TESTIFIES: NPCs in the next run react to it without knowing why. The Fold knows.
Q128.P5.title: THE PRIZE THAT SURVIVES THE ERASURE [W7, F9 fixed]

Q128.P6.body: Bohemia's warmest quests should end by asking the dynast to LEAVE — the reward room's final verb is the door. Cross-ref Q108's corner reunion: 2nd confirmation of UNCENTERED PAYOFFS: the best thing that happens is not about you, and the staging says so.
Q128.P6.title: THE WITNESS DISMISSED [W5]

Q128.W1.body: Keys are appointments; walls are other people's schedules; the map is a timetable. No quest in the corpus builds its entire challenge from WHEN.
Q128.W1.title: THE CLOCK IS THE DUNGEON

Q128.W10.body: The final hour's staging — vows under the falling moon — is the medium's cleanest statement that meaning is a thing people do at deadlines, not after them.
Q128.W10.title: THE END OF THE WORLD ATTENDS A WEDDING

Q128.W2.body: The postman delivers, the innkeeper checks in guests, the thief robs — the world ends in three days and everyone clocks in. Routine as courage, and as denial; the quest refuses to rule which.
Q128.W2.title: EVERYONE KEEPS THEIR SCHEDULE INTO THE APOCALYPSE

Q128.W3.body: The pendant delivered, Anju chooses to stay in a doomed town for a maybe. The player enables the bravest decision in the game and is not consulted on it.
Q128.W3.title: THE MIDPOINT IS A WOMAN DECLINING RESCUE

Q128.W4.body: Kafei's arc has no persuasion node — he is not talked out of hiding; he keeps an appointment as he is. Arrival is the apology.
Q128.W4.title: SHAME IS DEFEATED BY PUNCTUALITY

Q128.W5.body: The quest's final beat excludes its player: the Couple's Mask is handed over and the door is closed. Witness, then absence — the reward includes being dismissed from it.
Q128.W5.title: THE WEDDING ASKS YOU TO LEAVE

Q128.W6.body: Miss an hour and no screen tells you; the world just quietly holds its sadder configuration. The chain fails the way real plans fail: without ceremony.
Q128.W6.title: FAILURE IS AMBIENT

Q128.W7.body: Rewind to save the world and only the mask and the player remember. The quest gives the player a memory with no witnesses — carrying it IS the reward's final form.
Q128.W7.title: THE PRIZE SURVIVES THE ERASURE AND THE MARRIAGE DOESN'T

Q128.W8.body: His final choice (flee vs finish the route) compresses the quest's whole argument about duty and terror into one uniformed man reading his own regulations for permission to be afraid.
Q128.W8.title: THE POSTMAN IS THE THESIS IN MINIATURE

Q128.W9.body: The chain's crucial links are LETTERS with collection times — intimacy routed through infrastructure. The corpus's best marriage of logistics and longing (cf. Q101's supply-chain rescue: this is the supply chain OF a rescue of a marriage).
Q128.W9.title: HOPE TRAVELS BY MAIL

Q128.X1.body: Three days of exact hours across a dozen locations: the community verdict for 25 years is that blind completion is near-mythical. Theme-in-optional's terminal form: THEME-IN-SCHEDULING. LAW: clock-gated chains need in-world timetable objects (the Bombers' Notebook helps; it arrived undercooked).
Q128.X1.title: THE GUIDE PROBLEM

Q128.X10.body: Every retry replays known beats in real time; the quest's respect for schedules extends to punishing yours.
Q128.X10.title: THREE-DAY REPETITION FATIGUE

Q128.X2.body: No fail-state announcement is thematically perfect and practically brutal; players lose the chain without learning they lost it. LAW: ambience-failure needs one diegetic tell per broken link.
Q128.X2.title: SILENT FAILURE CUTS BOTH WAYS

Q128.X3.body: The Sakon hideout sequence bolts an execution test onto a scheduling quest; failure there wastes three real-time days. Genre whiplash at the worst hour.
Q128.X3.title: THE TANDEM CORRIDOR IS A DEXTERITY SPIKE

Q128.X4.body: The game never once lets Anju or Kafei sense the erasure; only the mask and the player carry it. Half the corpus would call that the point; bank the dissent.
Q128.X4.title: THE REWIND TAX IS UNDER-ACKNOWLEDGED

Q128.X5.body: The evacuation counsel is the survival play; the quest frames it as faithlessness. LAW: the sensible coward deserves one scene of vindication-adjacent dignity (cf. Q126 F3's unanimous chorus, inverted).
Q128.X5.title: ANJU'S MOTHER IS RIGHT AND UNREWARDED

Q128.X6.body: Who cursed him and why (Skull Kid, offhand) is set dressing; the quest's engine never touches its own inciting magic.
Q128.X6.title: KAFEI'S CURSE IS A PLOT COUPON

Q128.X7.body: His flee-or-finish crisis is the quest's thesis in one NPC and it lives in a side-branch most players miss. The best line of the arc is missable postage.
Q128.X7.title: THE POSTMAN STEALS THE THEME

Q128.X8.body: Anju trusts the mask's face; the quest never prices what it means that hope will follow a costume. Bohemia MUST price this (the Amalgamation is made of resemblances).
Q128.X8.title: RESEMBLANCE-TRUST IS UNEXAMINED

Q128.X9.body: The Couple's Mask opens one door in the main game; the artifact that survives a timeline does almost nothing mechanically. LAW: relics that survive erasure should testify somewhere.
Q128.X9.title: THE REWARD MASK IS UNDERUSED

Q129.N1.body: the intercom, entry: approach > "What do you want in there anyway?" [gate: none] -> R_WANT — "same as anyone": the reasonable sentence, delivered in a tone the quest DARES you to hear > "They'll never let you in." [gate: none] -> R_THEN — the tunnel offer surfaces: "there's another way in" > (listen to the whole rant) [gate: none] SILENCE -> the tells are ALL HERE on day one — the revenge is pre-announced to anyone who lets him finish. THE FINDING: the massacre is FORESHADOWED IN THE OPEN and seventeen years of players missed it because the karma system's GOOD stamp on door three overrode their own reading. THE METER OUTSHOUTED THE TEXT.
Q129.N1.title: NODE ROY_GATE

Q129.N2.body: per resident, entry: door three chosen > [Speech] "He's a person, same as you." [gate: stat-in-source; .bq-converts to knows:their_lever] -> some yield > (expose Susan's affair) [gate: knows:affair] TRAP-THAT-IS-THE-GOOD-PATH -> eviction; the diplomacy road is paved with a blackmail brick and the karma system does not notice. Bank: THE GOOD DOOR'S DIRTY HINGE — audit every "pure" path for the coercion it quietly includes. NOVERB: "Roy, will admission be ENOUGH?" — THE ONLY QUESTION THAT MATTERS HAS NO NODE. You can negotiate the tower and never once ask the wronged party what settlement actually settles. The absence IS the quest's argument: the broker never asked. Cross-ref Q121 (the heretics never consulted): 2nd confirmation of the ABSENT-PARTY DECISION — promote to law at compile: THE SETTLEMENT NOBODY ASKED THE WRONGED ABOUT WILL NOT HOLD.
Q129.N2.title: NODE THE_GAUNTLET

Q129.N3.body: the lobby, weeks later, entry: the return > "What did you do?" [gate: none] -> R_BREEZY — no denial, no gloat; mild. The register does the horror. > "I vouched for you." [gate: none] -> R_SO — your ledger is not his problem; he never signed YOUR moral paperwork > (draw) [gate: none] -> the kill with no quest attached: justice as a purely private line-item, unscored either way. NOVERB: (turn him in / restore anything) — NO RESTITUTION LAYER EXISTS. The world has no court for it, and the game's refusal to invent one is either its bravest beat or its laziest, and it will not tell you which.
Q129.N3.title: NODE ROY_AFTER

Q129.P1.title: THE SETTLEMENT NOBODY ASKED THE WRONGED ABOUT [core, NOVERB law]

Q129.P2.body: the 13 factions / tribunal / conscience One Bohemia integration quest per arc where the dynast can broker peace between a wronging faction and a wronged one — and the .bq DELIBERATELY OMITS the "will this be enough for you?" node unless the player has done the listening work ([gate: knows:their_grief] unlocks the one question that changes the outcome). Ask it and the settlement can hold; broker without it and the Tenpenny clock starts. The difference between the two runs is ONE conversation the format hides from the impatient.
Q129.P2.title: System

Q129.P3.body: Bohemia keeps the weeks-later massacre mechanic and fixes F1: the Fold receives ONE dated entry the day it happens ("basement. eleven. R. said it was owed."). Authorial fingerprint, diegetic, missable but findable — the subversion becomes provable without becoming announced.
Q129.P3.title: THE DELAYED DETONATION WITH FINGERPRINTS [F1 fixed]

Q129.P4.body: No meter in Bohemia, so the port is a WRITING law: no system stamp (reward, faction number, title) may fire at a settlement's HANDSHAKE — all pricing waits for the hold/collapse check one act later. Payment on OUTCOME, never on ceremony.
Q129.P4.title: THE METER THAT MISSES THE POINT [F2]

Q129.P5.body: Every "clean" Bohemia resolution gets one audited coercion in its path, VISIBLE — the Fold logs the blackmail brick in the diplomacy road. The player who takes the high road learns what it was paved with.
Q129.P5.title: THE GOOD DOOR'S DIRTY HINGE [F3]

Q129.P6.body: Bessie's fix: the wronged faction's non-violent majority receives exactly one node — after the detonation, one of them asks the dynast: "did you think he spoke for us?" The absent party, present once, exactly too late.
Q129.P6.title: THE QUIET ONES GET ONE SCENE [F4 fixed]

Q129.W1.body: The quest prices diplomacy highest — most nodes, most legwork, most patience — and detonates it. Effort is not virtue; the corpus's harshest single lesson about player self-congratulation.
Q129.W1.title: THE EFFORTFUL DOOR IS THE TRAP

Q129.W10.body: "Quest Complete" fires at the handshake; the actual ending arrives weeks later, uncredited. The gap between the game's bookkeeping and the story's truth IS the design (and F1's razor: one fingerprint would have made it undeniable).
Q129.W10.title: THE QUEST COMPLETES BEFORE IT ENDS

Q129.W2.body: Roy tells you, at the gate, on day one, in tone if not in terms. The foreshadowing is drowned out by a UI element (the karma stamp). A meter can make players deaf.
Q129.W2.title: THE MASSACRE IS PRE-ANNOUNCED AND UNHEARD

Q129.W3.body: Doors two and three end in the same basement; the only variable is whose name is on the guest ledger and how long the lobby smelled like peace.
Q129.W3.title: CONVERGENT BODY COUNTS, DIVERGENT SIGNATURES

Q129.W4.body: Roy will not be the grateful beneficiary of your speech build. He had his own quest running the whole time, and yours was a component in it.
Q129.W4.title: THE WRONGED PARTY DECLINES YOUR ARC

Q129.W5.body: No objective sends you back; the truth is compensation-free archaeology (Q116's law, executed at settlement scale).
Q129.W5.title: THE RETURN IS UNMARKED

Q129.W6.body: Roy's breeziness outperforms any snarl; atrocity discussed in the tone of a satisfied tenant is the file's coldest instrument.
Q129.W6.title: THE REGISTER OF THE AFTERMATH IS MILD

Q129.W7.body: Kill Roy after and no system blesses or bills it — the one moment the karma engine's silence works FOR the scene: the player's response has no exchange rate.
Q129.W7.title: JUSTICE IS LEFT ENTIRELY PRIVATE

Q129.W8.body: The gauntlet decomposes "the tower won't allow it" into fourteen individually arguable humans — prejudice rendered as a canvassing problem, door by door.
Q129.W8.title: BIGOTRY IS ITEMIZED

Q129.W9.body: Tenpenny's shrug — sure, let them in, whatever — is the quest's sharpest political note: the owner never needed the bigotry; he just never needed to oppose it either.
Q129.W9.title: POWER IS INDIFFERENT, NOT HATEFUL

Q129.X1.body: Seventeen years of "is this intended?" threads; cut content suggests a stable-integration variant existed. LAW: a gut-punch must carry authorial fingerprints (one line, one note, one witness) or it reads as QA failure.
Q129.X1.title: THE SUBVERSION IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A BUG

Q129.X10.body: Masterpiece-read leans on Roy's foreshadowing; botch-read leans on the cut content; neither closes. Bank the undecidability itself as the design datum.
Q129.X10.title: BOTH READINGS REQUIRE THE OTHER'S EVIDENCE

Q129.X2.body: Good karma for the setup, zero movement on the massacre: the meter grades intentions and ignores outcomes, confessing its own uselessness. The no-karma tripod (Q121/Q125/Q105) gains a fourth leg: THE METER THAT MISSES THE POINT ENTIRELY.
Q129.X2.title: THE KARMA SYSTEM SLEEPS THROUGH THE ENDING

Q129.X3.body: The affair-exposure eviction sits inside the diplomacy route unexamined.
Q129.X3.title: THE GOOD PATH REQUIRES BLACKMAIL AND NOBODY NOTICES

Q129.X4.body: Bessie and the quiet ones are furniture to BOTH resolutions in their name — wronged-party interiority budget: one character, and he's the killer.
Q129.X4.title: ROY'S GHOULS GET NO VOTE

Q129.X5.body: The massacre fires on a hidden clock; players who never return never learn; the quest's entire point is missable by contentment. THEME-IN-RETURNING.
Q129.X5.title: THE TIMER IS OPAQUE

Q129.X6.body: Every yielding resident yields to leverage or fatigue, never to argument that lands; the gauntlet proves speech checks move people without CHANGING them — which is the point, and is also never surfaced.
Q129.X6.title: NO RESIDENT IS PERSUADABLE ABOUT THE RIGHT THING

Q129.X7.body: The owner's indifference is never priced by any branch; the building's god outlives every configuration of its tenants (absent an unrelated sniper option elsewhere).
Q129.X7.title: TENPENNY HIMSELF ESCAPES THE THEME

Q129.X8.body: Residents pushed out for the deal exit the simulation; the diplomacy route's own displaced have no downstream existence.
Q129.X8.title: THE EVICTED VANISH

Q129.X9.body: The player's only processing tools are a gun and a fast-travel map; companions don't comment; the world doesn't reference it. The loudest silence in the game.
Q129.X9.title: MORAL AFTERSHOCK HAS NO MECHANICAL HOME

Q130.N1.body: entry: the note followed > "Who's watching you?" [gate: none] -> G_EVERYONE — the roster; the certainty; the gold > "You need a healer, not a spy." [gate: none] TRAP-OF-HONESTY -> G_RECOIL — early truth closes the quest's interior; he finds another instrument or worse. THE FINDING: THE HELP-VERB FIRES BLANKS AT PARANOIA — the honest sentence is not wrong, it is USELESS, and the quest prices the difference. > (take the gold) [gate: none] -> the tails begin NOVERB: "What if you're wrong?" — THE HYPOTHESIS IS UNHOSTABLE. His frame has no slot for it; the dialogue simply lacks the node, because HE lacks the node. INTERFACE AS PSYCHOLOGY (cf. Q98's procedural composure): the option list IS the character's epistemology. Bank as the file's core: WRITE THE CLIENT'S DIALOGUE OPTIONS FROM INSIDE THEIR MODEL.
Q130.N1.title: NODE CHAPEL_MIDNIGHT

Q130.N2.body: each dawn, entry: tail complete > "She's innocent. It's gardening." [gate: knows:the_truth] TRUTH-AS-RISK -> his ledger moves — toward doubt of YOU, not of the premise. Truth spends YOUR credibility, not his theory's. > "You were right. She's in on it." [gate: none] LIE-AS-FUEL -> gold now, a name on a list later. The lie is FRICTIONLESS at point of sale; the invoice arrives in stage 5A with an axe or a contract. > "I need more time." [gate: none] STALL -> the meter holds; the madman is MANAGEABLE, indefinitely, for anyone willing to make a client of him. THE THIRD OPTION IS THE DARKEST: maintenance. Nobody dies and nothing heals and the gold keeps coming.
Q130.N2.title: NODE THE_REPORT

Q130.N3.body: entry: three confirmations > (take the contract) [gate: none] -> three innocent-murders, paid; the karma system notices THESE (the meter that slept through Tenpenny wakes for retail murder — bank the inconsistency) > "No. This ends." [gate: none] -> the axe at midnight; self-defense as the quest's forced closer > (to the guard) [gate: none] -> Dion's sword or cell; the institution's mercy has exactly the granularity institutions have
Q130.N3.title: NODE THE_LIST

Q130.P1.title: THE CLIENT WHOSE REALITY YOU WRITE [core]

Q130.P2.body: dialogue spec / conscience / the 13 factions One Bohemia client per act whose world-model is the actual quest terrain: reports write to their beliefs, beliefs write to their deeds, and the .bq models it as a visible-to-Claude, invisible-to-player LEDGER (@MODEL lines on the client: what they now believe, updated per report). F1's fix built in: every surveillance finds ONE ambiguous datum, honestly writable either way — confirmation becomes interpretation. [PENDING, Paolo's call.]
Q130.P2.title: System

Q130.P3.body: The Fold tracks a per-NPC CREDIBILITY line: honest corrections of a motivated believer SPEND it. Bohemia makes the real-world economics of truth-telling mechanical — and never editorializes about it.
Q130.P3.title: TRUTH BILLED TO THE TELLER [W3]

Q130.P4.body: The stall-state gets one discovery hook (a townsperson: "he's had 'investigators' before, you know") so the darkest branch is findable. The Fold logs maintenance income under its own heading. The ledger calls it what it is; no one else does.
Q130.P4.title: THE MAINTENANCE BRANCH, NAMED [W5, F3 fixed]

Q130.P5.body: Bohemia's tails have counter-surveillance: targets notice on a schedule; being seen following writes ITS own consequences. Surveillance becomes a two-ledger game — direct feed for the occupancy/schedule plumbing already in the engine.
Q130.P5.title: THE WATCHED WORLD WATCHES BACK [F8 fixed]

Q130.P6.body: The NETWORK's threat-model is a paranoid client with infrastructure: it pays (in access, in power) for CONFIRMATIONS of threats to itself, and the dynast's reports write to a machine's world-model with a city attached. The Q130 machine, industrialized: what the Amalgamation believes about the settlement is partly player-authored, and the axe it eventually swings was loaded one report at a time. [PENDING, Paolo's call — this is an Act-2/3 spine candidate.]
Q130.P6.title: THE AMALGAMATION AS GLARTHIR AT SCALE [the lore port]

Q130.W1.body: Reports are writes to a man's world-model, and the model has a body count. No quest in the corpus makes the pen this literal.
Q130.W1.title: THE CLIENT'S REALITY IS PLAYER-WRITABLE

Q130.W10.body: Every corpse in every branch is optional and authored; the quest's violence is 100% player-written through an intermediary who believes you. Responsibility with one layer of laundering — and the laundering is the lesson.
Q130.W10.title: NOBODY HAS TO DIE AND SOMEONE USUALLY DOES

Q130.W2.body: You WATCH the innocence for three days before any node lets you deny it — the tails are the evidence; the reports are the confession.
Q130.W2.title: THE GAMEPLAY TEACHES THE TRUTH BEFORE THE FORK ASKS

Q130.W3.body: Honest reports spend your standing in his ledger, not his theory's. The corpus's cleanest model of why people stop correcting the paranoid: correction is expensive and billed to the corrector.
Q130.W3.title: TRUTH COSTS THE TRUTH-TELLER

Q130.W4.body: Confirmation costs one dialogue click and pays gold; the invoice arrives days later with names on it. Fear-feeding priced exactly like real life: cheap now, catastrophic on delivery.
Q130.W4.title: THE LIE IS FRICTIONLESS AT POINT OF SALE

Q130.W5.body: The stall — managing a sick man forever for coin, curing nothing, killing no one — is the quest's darkest mirror and it's just... available, unmarked, indefinitely.
Q130.W5.title: MAINTENANCE IS A BRANCH

Q130.W6.body: "What if you're wrong" is absent because HE has no slot for it; the option list is a psychograph. Interface as the client's mind.
Q130.W6.title: THE HYPOTHESIS HAS NO NODE

Q130.W7.body: "You need a healer" is true, kind, and useless — the quest lets decency be correct and ineffective at once, which almost nothing in the medium permits.
Q130.W7.title: THE HELP-VERB FIRES BLANKS

Q130.W8.body: The guard exit works and is exactly as gentle as a city watch gets: the honest price of outsourcing a sick man to public order.
Q130.W8.title: THE INSTITUTION'S MERCY HAS INSTITUTIONAL GRANULARITY

Q130.W9.body: Chapel shadows, passed notes, dawn drops — the quest wraps you in the paranoid's dramaturgy until following his stagecraft feels like procedure. Form as contagion.
Q130.W9.title: THE MIDNIGHT STAGING IS THE DIAGNOSIS

Q130.X1.body: The game never permits the tails to find ANYTHING ambiguous; the player's knowledge is total, which makes the lie-branch pure villainy instead of judgment under uncertainty. LAW: the surveillance should find ONE genuinely odd datum per target — writable either way — so confirmation becomes interpretation, not fabrication.
Q130.X1.title: THE TARGETS ARE CERTIFIED INNOCENT

Q130.X10.body: Whoever dies, Skingrad resumes; no funeral, no gossip-state, no guard-log entry readable later. The town has no memory organ (the anti-Fold).
Q130.X10.title: AFTERMATH IS A ZERO

Q130.X2.body: The quest uses paranoia as a plot engine and exits through an axe; no branch models care beyond the guard's blade. Period-typical, banked as such, not excused.
Q130.X2.title: GLARTHIR'S ILLNESS IS A MONSTER COSTUME

Q130.X3.body: Indefinite management — the most interesting exit — is undiscoverable except by accident; no rumor, no node names it.
Q130.X3.title: THE STALL BRANCH IS INVISIBLE

Q130.X4.body: The meter's selective hearing, exhibit N.
Q130.X4.title: THE KARMA WAKES INCONSISTENTLY (see node note): sleeping through brokered massacres elsewhere, alert to these retail ones

Q130.X5.body: Following schedules in Oblivion is walking slowly behind a pathing NPC; the surveillance fantasy outruns its verbs.
Q130.X5.title: THE TAILS ARE MECHANICALLY THIN

Q130.X6.body: That honest reports move suspicion onto YOU is discoverable only by suffering it; one in-world hint exists (townsfolk warnings), thin.
Q130.X6.title: TRUTH'S COST IS UNDER-TELEGRAPHED

Q130.X7.body: One sentence to Dion closes the whole machine at any point; the institutional door has no toll (cf. Q126 F7's four-bypass gate).
Q130.X7.title: THE GUARD EXIT IS TOO CHEAP

Q130.X8.body: Three days of being followed by an armored stranger registers with no one; the watched world doesn't watch back.
Q130.X8.title: NO NEIGHBOR EVER NOTICES THE TAIL

Q130.X9.body: Payment scales with confirmations; the economy editorializes toward the lie (reward-gradient law, Q121's corollary, violated here in the WRONG direction on purpose or not — undecidable, banked).
Q130.X9.title: THE GOLD CURVE REWARDS FEEDING THE FEAR

Q131.N1.body: the shrine, entry: arrival among the corpses > "Why someone who trusts me?" [gate: none] -> B_BECAUSE — strangers cost nothing; the Prince buys only what hurts to sell > "And if I refuse?" [gate: none] -> B_INDIFFERENT — the quest simply waits, forever, in the journal; refusal is free and the entry never leaves. THE OPEN QUEST AS STANDING TEMPTATION (cf. Q126 W3's unexpiring offer — here the offer sits in your own journal for the rest of the game, a to-do item made of a person). NOVERB: "Take me instead." — SELF-SACRIFICE IS NOT PURCHASABLE. The Prince has no use for what you'd volunteer; only what someone else volunteered TO YOU. The removed verb defines the commodity: trust is only spendable by its custodian, never by its owner.
Q131.N1.title: NODE THE_TERMS

Q131.N2.body: the pillar, entry: follower present This is the quest's entire conversation and it is a UI gesture: > "I need you to do something." -> (point at pillar) -> they walk, they touch, they hang. > (release them instead) [gate: none] EXIT-AT-THE-ALTAR -> the command wheel works BOTH ways to the last second; standing down is one click cheaper than the murder. The quest keeps the exit open at maximal proximity — you can bring someone to the altar, watch them bound, and STILL walk it back (dismiss, unbind by leaving). THE FINDING: THE LAST EXIT IS AT THE ALTAR ITSELF, and its availability makes completion a choice renewed at every step, not a slope (the anti-Sinnerman: Q122's fifty exits COMPRESSED into one continuously-open door). NOVERB: (explain / apologize / warn) — THE FOLLOWER HAS NO RECEIVING NODE. No dialogue exists to tell them what's happening, before or during. The game denies the betrayer the relief of confession (cf. Q4's Downwarren: no confession verb — 2nd confirmation; betrayal must be carried silent).
Q131.N2.title: NODE THE_COMMAND

Q131.N3.body: entry: the blow landed The Prince animates your follower's body to congratulate you. > (listen) [gate: none] -> the speech in the borrowed voice: the quest's cruelest staging decision — approval delivered through the instrument of its price. > (attack the corpse-puppet) [gate: none] -> futile; the Prince is not IN reach; you can only hit what's left of your friend. The rage-verb exists and lands on exactly the wrong body.
Q131.N3.title: NODE BOETHIAH_THROUGH_THE_CORPSE

Q131.P2.body: companions / the Amalgamation / conscience One Bohemia offer per generation priced specifically in a COMPANION THE SYSTEM VERIFIES TRUSTS THE DYNAST (bond-state gate, not any warm body — F5's fix: the .bq gates on [gate: bond:X>=n], unproxyable). The NETWORK's version: an upload slot that only accepts the willingly-brought. The Fold records WHO, forever, by name. F1's fix native: Bohemia's ledger cannot price a housecarl and a hireling identically because bond-state is real state.
Q131.P2.title: System

Q131.P3.body: Refused offers never leave the Fold's open-items list. One standing temptation per act, visible every time the ledger opens, undismissable. Refusal gets F7's fix too: at generation's end, ONE line acknowledges the never-taken deal. The Fold notices restraint.
Q131.P3.title: THE IMMORTAL OPEN ENTRY [W4]

Q131.P4.body: If Bohemia ever stages a betrayal quest, the LAW: it executes entirely through the companion-command verbs the player has used benignly all game. No new interface, no special scene — the horror is that nothing changed except intent. [PENDING, Paolo's call on whether Bohemia stages one at all.]
Q131.P4.title: BETRAYAL IN LOYALTY'S UI [W1]

Q131.P5.body: Any Bohemia item bought with a person carries its receipt diegetically: the item's [READ] entry names them; companions recognize it; one NPC per act refuses to trade while it's worn. The armor testifies (cf. Q128 PORT 4 — the testimony law's second pillar).
Q131.P5.title: THE RECEIPT-BEARING RELIC [F10, W10 fixed together]

Q131.P6.body: The Amalgamation already speaks through the uploaded dead. The port is the ESCALATION: after any dynast-authored death that feeds the NETWORK, the Amalgamation's next contact can arrive in THAT voice — approval, invoice, or greeting through the newest acquisition. Paolo's antagonist gets the corpus's cruelest staging trick as a standing capability. [PENDING, Paolo's call.]
